messages:
dave - Support: FYI Acme reporting the A/B dashboard shows swapped variant labels and assignment counts that don't match their server-side logs. Screenshot attached: https://redwood-internal.s3/bugs/acme-flip-7.png

acme-ops (customer): we're seeing about ~60% users in variant B on our side but your dashboard shows ~60% in variant A since 2024-11-02 03:00 UTC. This broke our analysis. :frowning:

elenor - Customer Success: Thanks for reporting — can you confirm experiment id and the exact time window you queried? Also does the discrepancy show in the raw "assignments" table export?

acme-ops (customer): exp_id=exp-acme-2024-11, window 2024-11-02T02:50..2024-11-02T04:30 UTC. I can share a CSV if needed.

dave - Support: @minh can you take a look? sounds like an analytics join issue (labels->variant_key mapping) after the dashboard change we shipped last night.

minh - Eng: looking. I pulled the raw assignment rows for that exp and time window — they match the customer's CSV: variant_key A=615, B=410. Dashboard shows A=412, B=623. That suggests label->key mapping inverted during aggregation.

minh - Eng: quick repro query I ran from the analytics DB:
```sql
-- counts from assignments table
SELECT variant_key, count(*) AS cnt
FROM inference_assignments
WHERE experiment_id='exp-acme-2024-11' AND ts >= '2024-11-02T02:50:00Z' AND ts <= '2024-11-02T04:30:00Z'
GROUP BY variant_key;
-- result: A | 615, B | 410

-- counts from dashboard aggregation path (post-join)
SELECT a.label, count(*) AS cnt
FROM inference_assignments ia
JOIN experiment_variants ev ON ia.variant_key = ev.key
WHERE ev.experiment_id='exp-acme-2024-11' AND ia.ts >= '2024-11-02T02:50:00Z' AND ia.ts <= '2024-11-02T04:30:00Z'
GROUP BY a.label;
-- result (what dashboard shows): A | 412, B | 623
```

minh - Eng: root cause hypothesis: our dashboard aggregation service switched to joining on ev.normalized_label in a PR last night (to support label-casing), but for experiments created before the normalization code path ev.key vs ev.normalized_label can collide when labels are non-unique across namespaces. In short, the join isn't using the canonical variant_key in some code paths.

jorge - Product: Which PR? any rollout flags we can flip quickly? Customers are already on calls.

minh - Eng: PR #1189 — it was behind a feature-flag (agg-label-normalization) but it looks like the flag defaulted to ON in prod for analytics-api after the deploy. I can flip the flag back to OFF for analytics-api, that should restore previous behaviour immediately.

dave - Support: Please do that and confirm with Acme. Also we should add a smoke-check to compare raw assignment counts vs aggregated counts for experiments over the last hour.

minh - Eng: rolling back the feature-flag now.

eng-release-bot: Deployed change: analytics-api.feature_flags.agg-label-normalization -> OFF by minh at 2024-11-02T05:12:34Z :white_check_mark:

minh - Eng: After flipping, I re-ran the aggregation query — counts now match the assignments table (A=615, B=410). Pushing a quick hotfix to ensure join always uses variant_key regardless of normalization flag.

elenor - Customer Success: @acme-ops can you verify dashboard numbers now?

acme-ops (customer): checked — dashboard matches our logs now. Thanks.

jorge - Product: action items: 1) revert PR #1189 or fix join to use canonical key (minh) 2) add rollout gating to default feature-flag state (minh) 3) add hourly smoke-compare check between assignments table and dashboard aggregates (dave/eng-sre) 4) notify customers affected and postmortem (elenor/jorge).

minh - Eng: filed bug: ENG-4573, pushing hotfix and unit tests. Will follow up with postmortem tomorrow.

dave - Support: tagging this resolved for now, keeping thread open until postmortem. :eyes:
